tag: EP.14A · How to Support a Breath
title: How to Support a Breath

beats.t: In the bakery attic, Yundal unfolded a sheet of paper on a table made of stacked flour sacks. It showed a charcoal cross section of the clock tower.
The vault has seven levels beneath the clock tower. The deeper you go, the slower time moves.
By the last chamber, a single step takes about an hour. One breath could take a day.
So if you sneeze down there, you lose a week?
Hold in your sneezes. Especially you, Moka.
Why especially me?
Otters have sensitive noses. Oh, speaking of which, what time were you born, Moka?
You're asking an otter his birth time at a moment like this? One star.
That's a habit of yours, isn't it? Asking everyone you meet.
Occupational hazard. Once I know someone's birth hour, I can see where they're likely to stumble.
I keep stumbling at the seventh chamber. Time has almost stopped there.
Ordinary breathing won't sustain you there. Your breath freezes and catches in your chest.
Your breath freezes? Then how do we get in?
Support it. Hold it up from underneath so it doesn't fall.
Before that, let's assign our roles. Moka, you'll lure the guards at the entrance with food smells.
What are the guards? Rabbits?
People who couldn't repay their time. They stand guard outside the vault to pay their debts. They'll be hungry. They've been hungry a very long time.
Then I'm feeding them, not luring them. That I can do.
Moka's whiskers drooped, then rose again. He seemed to be remembering the faces of the people on the Island of Expression who had lost their sense of taste.
Mr. Cat opens the way, I eat the locked doors, and our lady goes to the deepest chamber.
Why do I have to go deepest?
The seventh chamber only opens with time you've earned yourself. You're the only one of us who has any.
(My twelve minutes.)
Yeoni covered the small writing on one hoof with the other. The twelve minutes they had meant to frame suddenly felt heavy.
Can I review this plan? Five stars for recklessness, three for detail. I can't give the survival rate a rating yet.
An honest review. The best I've had in three years.
On the roof, the island's ticking grew distant. Yeongnyangi sat facing Yeoni and held out a paw.
Rest your hoof on my paw. Press lightly as you breathe in, and don't lift it when you breathe out. Let's try it together.
Press, don't let go. Got it. Seems easy enough.
The first breath was easy. On the second, the center of Yeoni's chest began to ache. On the third, their hoof slipped.
Not easy at all. My breath keeps running upward.
Because you're pulling it up. Don't tug at it. Set it down on the ground.
(Don't tug at it. I've heard that somewhere before.)
Yeoni closed their eyes. They sent the breath down below their belly, instead of into their chest. Yeongnyangi's paw supported it from beneath.
A pale green shoot sprouted from the tip of Yeoni's hoof. It slowly wound its way up over Yeongnyangi's paw.
I did it! Did you see? A sprout!
At that moment, silver flashed from Yeongnyangi's paw. The climbing shoot was silently severed and fell to the roof.
Uh... why did it get cut?
My energy is Metal. A power that can cut Wood.
Remember that. Mine is an energy that hurts you. The closer you get, the more it does.
But you just supported my breath. Would an energy that hurts me hold me up like that?
That's...
You can't answer, can you? Then I'll go with my interpretation. Half cutting, half supporting.
Instead of answering, Yeongnyangi picked up the severed sprout and tucked it behind Yeoni's ear.
Is this... a decoration? Like a ribbon?
Keep it as evidence. So you can't change your story later about getting hurt in training.
First cat I've ever seen tuck evidence behind someone's ear. Four stars.
Why deduct one?
Your explanation was too short.
Beneath the attic window, Moka clicked his tongue as he turned a skewer. Are those two training or dating?
We can hear you! We're training! I've even got evidence!
After Yeoni went back down to the attic, Yeongnyangi stayed at the roof's edge. In the moonlight, he turned his left paw over.
The fur on its underside was burned in patches, scorched in the crow's courtroom. Green sap from the sprout had spread over the wound.
That paw still hasn't healed.
How long have you been watching?
Since we first met in the tent. Whenever you take a step, your left paw is always half a beat late.
Hurting Officer is strong in our lady's chart. The energy that makes words into fire. The stronger that fire grows, the more it hurts the Officer.
Don't say who that Officer is. Not to Yeoni, either.
If you don't say it, it'll all come out someday. Hiding a wound doesn't make it smaller.
I know. But not now. I don't want Yeoni to become afraid of their own fire.
Yundal watched Yeongnyangi's profile for a while. The cat's violet eyes spread into gold, fixed only on the light in the attic window.
Keeping a secret is expensive. Your birth hour should cover it, Mr. Cat.
I don't know it. My birthday.
You really don't know? I thought you were joking yesterday.
Yundal stopped smiling and patted Yeongnyangi's shoulder once with his gloved hand.
All right. I'll put it on your tab. My whole life's on credit, too. I know the feeling.
At two in the morning, the four gathered in the shadows of the square beneath the clock tower. Its hands turned sluggishly overhead.
Forty skewers for the scent diversion. Twenty spicy, twenty sweet.
Luna's sister has four hours left. We get out before sunrise.
[ Luna's sister · Today remaining: 03:58:12 ]
Don't forget how to support your breath.
How could I? I've got the evidence tucked behind my ear.
Yeoni looked up at the clock tower. Nobody stood on its hands. That was even more frightening.
The tiger is below. A vault keeper doesn't leave its vault.
Those stripes. That's the one that collected the applause on the Island of Expression. This time, it's my turn.
We're not going to fight. We're going to get things back.
Remember those words in the seventh chamber, too.
Yundal adjusted his glove. His fingertips trembled ever so slightly.
Let's find your name, too. Once we do, I'll be the first to call you by it.
Then you'll be the third person to say my name, my lady.
Why third?
First my mother, second me. Then you.
The tower bell rang twice. Following the shadows, the four slipped through the clock tower door.
